title: Edge Latency Bridge - Weekly Sync Prep (Z. Martinez)
body:
Purpose:
- Prep notes for the weekly trilateral sync (Serving Runtime / Infrastructure / Console). Aim: short alignment, surface risks for the Canary rollout of edge-cache, confirm dashboard readiness, and allocate owners for follow-ups. Keep meeting to 40 minutes (timeboxed).

Fast facts (snapshot):
- Canary cluster x-edge-2 running since 2026-03-06.
- Production p50: 18ms token; p95: 142ms token (global aggregate).
- Canary p50: 16ms token; p95: 110ms token (slightly better but noisy in ASIA region).
- Error spike: Mar 10 02:14 UTC ~ 0.7% 5xx on x-edge-2 for ~12m (suspect KV cache miss storm).

Agenda (40m total):
1) Quick roll call + goals (3m) — Zoe
2) Canary health & metrics highlights (8m) — Arjun
   - Confirm p95 trend on canary vs prod (show graph CON-2184).
   - Call out ASIA tail: sample traces attached in PR 891.
3) Incident recap: Mar 10 error spike (7m) — Lena
   - Root-cause hypothesis: concurrent prefix flush while autoscaler triggered new workers.
   - Short-term mitigation applied: increased backoff in KV client (deployed 03-10 03:02 UTC).
4) Console rollout checklist & dashboard readiness (7m) — Mikael
   - Verify token-level breakdown and trace links are enabled for canary.
5) Infra & autoscale tuning (7m) — Priya
   - Discuss proposal to add a 30s stabilization window to autoscaler to avoid thrash.
6) Action item review + owners + due dates (5m) — Zoe
   - Rapid confirmations, any blockers, and parking lot.

Pre-meeting prep: (what I will bring)
- Short clip of the ASIA tail traces + trace ids (copy into Slack thread).
- Quick screenshot of CON-2184 dashboard showing last 72h p95.
- Draft autoscale stabilization config (k8s HPA/cluster-autoscaler suggestion).

Open questions to flag in the meeting:
- Is the 30s stabilization window acceptable for latency-sensitive tenants? (Priya to quantify impact in staging).
- Should we throttle prefix flushes at runtime or gate them behind a maintenance window? (trade-offs: latency vs stale KV).
- Do we have sufficient tracing correlation between Console routes and runtime requests for the canary? (Mikael to confirm sampling rate).

Action items (working tracker) — short IDs so we can reference in followups:
- AI-101: Run a focused replay of the Mar 10 02:00-02:30 UTC window against canary with logging level DEBUG to capture KV client state. Owner: Arjun. Due: 2026-03-14. Status: in_progress. Linked: INF-4320.
- AI-102: Add 30s stabilization window proposal PR to infra repo + perf benchmark results (staging). Owner: Priya. Due: 2026-03-16. Status: todo. Linked: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-configs/pull/72.
- AI-103: Console: enable trace link for canary routes and add one-click jump from token row to trace viewer. Owner: Mikael. Due: 2026-03-15. Status: todo. Linked: CON-2184.
- AI-104: Instrument a lightweight KV miss metric (per-prefix) and surface as alert (p95 spike > 30% of baseline). Owner: Lena. Due: 2026-03-18. Status: todo. Linked: INF-4320.
- AI-105: Draft communications blurb for customers if the canary is promoted and we expect brief tail risk; include rollback playbook summary. Owner: Zoe. Due: 2026-03-17. Status: todo. Linked: DOC-comm-661.

Notes to self (fragments / scratch):
- Bring sample trace id: 8f9b2a (was noisy, confirm exact two-digit suffix).
- Check if PR 891 has the updated backoff constants we rolled out; might need a follow-up patch.
- Ask SRE on call about any infra changes at 02:00 UTC on Mar 10 (could be unrelated).
- Consider adding synthetic test that simulates concurrent prefix flush + burst traffic. Put in backlog if not urgent.

Parking lot (if time):
- Long-term: evaluate prefix sharding to reduce hot-spotting for certain long-running prompts. (Research task).
- Explore kv-cache local replication strategy for ASIA region to reduce tail.

Post-meeting follow-up template (copy/paste after meeting):
- TL;DR (1–2 lines): what we decided.
- Owner: list of action items with owners and due dates.
- Blockers: any follow-ons.
- Next check-in: date/time for progress sync.

Quick calendar note: schedule 30m follow-up on 2026-03-17 to review AI-101/102 progress (proposed).

Draft email blurb for follow-up (for later):
"Thanks all — short recap from today's Edge Latency Bridge sync: we confirmed the canary is overall healthier than prod but saw an ASIA tail spike on Mar 10 linked to a KV miss storm. Agreed next steps: Arjun to run a focused replay, Priya to propose a stabilization window, Mikael to enable trace links, Lena to add KV miss metric, and Zoe to draft the customer-facing blurb. Targets above. If you pick up any AI, mark it in JIRA and update the tracker. I'll post the meeting notes and files in the CON-2184 page."

End of prep notes.

-- Z.
